part: Section/panel card — the list surfaces' rail card (ruling 5.1)
source: docs/design/handoff-2026-09-06/README.md §0.4 (rail labels convention); 'Caros Ledge UI System.dc.html' the Legend rail card shared by artboards 02/04/06/08/11; operator ruling 5.1 ('the graduated rule ABOVE the section title wins... Applies to every panel/section card on every page')
notes: ListSurfaceRailCards.tsx (RailCard, used by LegendRailCard and every other rail card the five list surfaces render) is pure inline style; every property here is a real product value.

This is the ONE panel/section card shape shared by all five list surfaces (Regulations/Market/Research/Operations/Watchlist) that carries a visible title — the OTHER card on those pages (ListSurfaceShell's per-band grouping, `BandSectionHeader`) uses its own distinct convention (a coloured 3px TOP-BORDER per band, `borderTop:'3px solid '+band.cssVar`, README §0.2's band scale, not ruling 5.1's dark-grey gradation) and is NOT this ruling's target — a band subsection is not a titled panel in the ruling's sense, it is the list's own per-band grouping, unchanged by this ruling.

Ruling 5.1: 'the graduated rule ABOVE the section title wins. 3px, full width of the card, top edge, no radius on it, and NO line below the title... Applies to every panel/section card on every page.' RailCard.tsx renders NO rule above its title at all — no `
` of any height/background before the `

` title — which is why the target below reports NOT BUILT rather than a coloured/positioned MISMATCH: there is no element to measure a colour on.

The title itself ('Legend') is styled 10.5px/800/.12em uppercase — README §0.4's RAIL LABEL convention, not the Anton section-title convention ruling 5.1 also states ('Section title itself: Anton uppercase, no divider, no underline'). Whether a rail card's meta-style label counts as ruling 5.1's 'section title' (requiring Anton) is not resolved by the ruling's own wording — it names the DASHBOARD's own primary section titles ('Due Next', 'By Urgency') as its worked example, and a rail card's compact label is a documented, PRE-EXISTING distinct convention (README type scale: 'rail labels 10.5px uppercase .12em/700'), so this is logged as an open question for the fix lane rather than asserted as a MISMATCH against a scale the ruling did not clearly extend to this element.
